ownership.notes: Delaware corporation (CIK 1176948; Ares Management, L.P. until November 2018); fiscal year ends 31 December. Its principal executive office is in Los Angeles, though its filings also refer to its New York headquarters. On a fully exchanged basis at 31 December 2025, Ares Owners Holdings L.P. held 32.54%, SMBC 5.02% and public holders 62.44% (10-K). Its 6.75% Series B mandatory convertible preferred trades as ARES.PRB.

summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Ares is a credit-first manager whose infrastructure arm reaches this corpus in two ways. The first is **Ada Infrastructure**, its own wholly owned data-centre development and operating platform, acquired with GLP Capital Partners' international business in March 2025. Ada reports more than 1 GW of campuses under way in Northern Virginia, Tokyo, Osaka, London and Brazil and has its own energy-procurement lead. The second is a set of power positions held by its funds. They control **Apex Clean Energy** (a majority since late 2021; two Ares partners on its board) and 80% of an EDPR California portfolio with 184 MW of batteries, and since 1 October 2026 Ares jointly controls Eni's Plenitude. Elsewhere Ares is a minority holder or lender. It shares joint control of Prime Data Centers, holds minority stakes (49% at EDPR) in operating renewables that ENGIE and EDPR run, holds preferred equity in SB Energy's parent (redeemed at the IPO) and roughly 10% of X-energy's votes (our calculation from its prospectus), and arranged a USD 2.4bn loan for Vantage.

**BACKGROUND.** Per company filings, the registrant is Ares Management Corporation (NYSE: ARES; CIK 1176948), a Delaware corporation reporting Credit, Real Assets (real estate and infrastructure), Secondaries and Private Equity. AUM was USD 671.3bn at 30 June 2026 (fee-paying USD 409.9bn), of which infrastructure was USD 29.9bn — about 4%. FY2025 after-tax realized income was USD 4.76 a share against a Zacks consensus of USD 5.07, a miss; Q2 2026's USD 1.29 met consensus. The company still expects over USD 350m of realized net performance income in 2026, but the first three quarters total about USD 136m on its own preliminary figures. The shares fell about 27% in 2026 to 2 October. Q3 results are due on 29 October 2026.
ecosystemRole: We assess Ares as a second-tier capital name that owns one real data-centre buyer outright and controls one real power buyer through its funds. Ada Infrastructure is Ares's own business, not a fund portfolio company: the 10-K calls it 'our dedicated data center operating platform', combining 'in-house data center development and operational expertise'. Its team includes a head of energy procurement and infrastructure, and it develops and operates the campuses of Ares's Japan DC Partners fund (about 240 MW in Greater Tokyo) and a 314-acre Spotsylvania, Virginia site. Apex Clean Energy is the funds' controlled power buyer: Apex's own management develops, builds and operates its wind, solar and storage projects and buys their equipment. Most other Ares energy exposure is passive — minority stakes beside ENGIE and EDPR (49% at EDPR), which operate, preferred equity, pipeline interests and lending.

productsAndServices.name: Ares Digital Infrastructure and Ada Infrastructure
productsAndServices.category: Data centres — in-house developer and operator
productsAndServices.description: Ares bought the international business of GLP Capital Partners ('GCP International') on 1 March 2025, for consideration with a fair value of USD 3.9bn (cash, Ares shares and contingent consideration), plus earnouts tied to the data-centre business and the Japan business capped at USD 1.0bn and USD 0.5bn. The deal brought Ada Infrastructure, which the 10-K calls 'our dedicated data center operating platform' inside a 'fully vertically-integrated' digital-infrastructure business. Ada reports eight in-flight campuses totalling over 1 GW of IT capacity: about 400 MW in Northern Virginia, five campuses of about 600 MW in Tokyo and Osaka, 210 MW in London and about 350 MW in Brazil.

productsAndServices.name: Ares Infrastructure Equity — power, renewables and midstream
productsAndServices.description: The former Energy Investors Funds, bought in 2015 and since renamed Infrastructure and Power, then Infrastructure Opportunities and now Infrastructure Equity, has 'roughly $15 billion deployed across over 60 investments'. Its funds have controlled Apex Clean Energy since a majority purchase announced in October 2021 and closed by the end of that year. They acquired 80% of an EDPR California portfolio of 200 MW of solar and 184 MW of batteries in September 2026 (about USD 0.8bn for 100% at the start of operations). They hold 49% of a 1,632 MW EDPR portfolio (about USD 2.9bn for 100%, October 2025) and successive minority stakes in ENGIE North America portfolios, which ENGIE continues to control and operate.

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **Ares is mostly a directory of buyers — with one door it owns**. Ares Management Corporation places no orders for power equipment, but Ada Infrastructure is its own platform, not a portfolio company, and Ada's energy-procurement and design leads specify and buy for the campuses Ares funds own. Basis: the 10-K's description of Ada as 'our dedicated data center operating platform' and Ada's published leadership. Apex Clean Energy is the funds' other controlled buyer, run by its own management.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **most of Ares's power exposure is passive capital recycled out of utilities and IPPs**. Basis: ENGIE's releases say it keeps control and operations of the portfolios Ares bought into; EDPR keeps 51% of the 1,632 MW portfolio; Rover and the Central Penn Line are operated by others; SB Energy's preferred and the Vantage loan are financing. The exceptions are Apex, the EDPR California batteries (80%) and Plenitude (joint control).

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Ada is Ares's AI-infrastructure growth engine, and Japan is its proof point**. Basis: Japan DC Partners I raised about USD 2.4bn for ~240 MW and booked USD 54.3m of carried interest in H1 2026 on a data-centre revaluation; the GCP earnouts — up to USD 1.0bn on the data-centre business — pay out only if the digital-infrastructure funds hit revenue targets. Ada's US entry at Spotsylvania (200 MW phase one) is the next test.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Ares's 2026 earnings story turns on performance income, not fees**. Basis: fee-related earnings grew about 20% to Q2, but realized net performance income totalled about USD 136m through Q3 on Ares's preliminary figures against a USD 350m-plus expectation, and FY2025 missed consensus on the same line. The shares fell about 27% in 2026 amid private-credit concerns and redemption caps at Ares Strategic Income Fund.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that **Prime Data Centers is not an Ares-controlled buyer today**, despite the 2025 joint-control clearance. Basis: Macquarie has sold out without naming the buyer, and Grain's April 2026 release calls Data Realty Holding Corp. Prime's 'controlling shareholder'; Ares keeps a board seat. No filing settles who controls Prime.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *Q3 2026 results, 29 October:* whether the USD 350m performance-income expectation is cut. *An Apex corporate-stake sale:* the outcome of the reported Lazard process. *Ada's first named power-equipment supplier or US tenant at Spotsylvania.* *The SB Energy IPO pricing:* triggers the redemption of Ares's preferred. *Ares Strategic Income Fund Q4 requests:* below 10% would ease the redemption pressure.

relationships.via: Ares Infrastructure Equity funds (formerly Infrastructure and Power)
relationships.note: Funds managed by Ares's infrastructure strategy have held a majority of Apex Clean Energy since a purchase announced in October 2021; two Ares partners sit on Apex's board.
relationships.context:
Apex's release of 6 October 2021 said funds and other accounts managed by Ares' Infrastructure and Power strategy had agreed to acquire a majority stake, closing before the end of 2021, with Apex's management continuing to lead the company. Ares has published nothing on Apex since; Keith Derman and Steven Porto list Apex board seats in their Ares bios, and PV Tech on 29 September 2026 still described Apex as majority-owned by Ares-managed funds.

ION Analytics reported on 4 December 2025 that Ares was marketing a minority stake in Apex through Lazard; no outcome is on the record, and Apex's 2026 transactions are project-level selldowns. Apex's own management signs for its turbines and batteries.

relationships.scale: Joint control cleared by the European Commission (share undisclosed)
relationships.note: Ares acquired joint control of Prime Data Centers with Macquarie's holding company and Data Realty Group, cleared by the European Commission in March 2025; an Ares partner sits on Prime's board, and current control is not settled on the record.
relationships.context:
The Commission's decision M.11843 of 18 March 2025 records Ares Management Corporation, Wholesale DC Asset Holdings (ultimately controlled by Macquarie) and Data Realty Group acquiring joint control of Prime Data Centers LLC, previously jointly controlled by the latter two. Prime's July 2025 release names Macquarie Capital, Ares Management and Siemens Financial Services as existing investors.

Macquarie's FY26 annual report records that Macquarie Capital 'completed the sale of its remaining stake in Prime Data Centers', naming no buyer, and Grain Management's April 2026 release calls Data Realty Holding Corp. Prime's 'founding and controlling shareholder'. Ares's Steven Porto lists a Prime board seat. No filing read for this dossier states Ares's share or settles who controls Prime now.

relationships.scale: USD 800m of preferred equity issued (≈USD 996m liquidation preference at 31 Dec 2025) plus warrants
relationships.note: Ares affiliates hold preferred equity and warrants in SBE Global, SB Energy's direct parent, which the S-1 says are redeemed in full at the IPO; no board seat.
relationships.context: SB Energy's S-1/A No. 2 (21 September 2026): SBE Global issued USD 800m of preferred equity to Ares across 2022, 2024 and 2025, with an aggregate liquidation preference of about USD 996m at 31 December 2025, and warrants with the 2025 issuance. The preferred is 'not an obligation of, or equity interest in, SB Energy, Inc.' At the IPO it is to be redeemed in full and the warrants net-settled for about USD 40m, after which Ares 'will no longer hold any equity interest, preferred claim, or warrant position in SBE Global or any of its subsidiaries'. Board designation rights go to SoftBank and OpenAI. Preferred equity with senior economics, not control.

relationships.scale: 4.9% of Class A and 20.5% of Class B after the IPO
relationships.via: Ares X-Energy Holdings and co-investment vehicles
relationships.note: Ares affiliates are significant minority holders of X-energy, with two Ares partners on its board but no contractual nomination right in the prospectus.
relationships.context: X-energy's final prospectus (27 April 2026) lists entities affiliated with Ares holding 13,844,585 Class A shares (4.9%) and 24,418,756 Class B shares (20.5%) after the offering. Class B shares carry one vote each and no economic rights and vote with Class A, so by our calculation Ares holds roughly 10% of the combined vote. Ares's 13G (August 2026) reports 38,263,341 shares with shared voting power, 12.3% of Class A on an as-converted basis. Ares partners David Kaplan and Allyson Satin sit on the board. Ares Acquisition Corporation's 2022 SPAC merger agreement with X-energy was terminated in 2023.

relationships.scale: 905 MW for US$430m (March 2025); 730 MW, US$153m paid in 2025 and about US$280m scheduled for 2026
relationships.note: Ares infrastructure funds hold non-controlling interests in successive ENGIE North America renewables portfolios; ENGIE keeps a controlling share and operates the assets.
relationships.context: ENGIE North America's releases of 24 March 2025 (nearly 1 GW of solar and storage) and 13 January 2026 (730 MW of operating wind and solar in ERCOT) describe sales to Ares Management Infrastructure Opportunities funds and say 'ENGIE will retain a controlling share in the portfolio and will continue to operate and manage the assets'. ENGIE SA's 2025 annual report (Note 16.2.4) gives the prices: US$430m for a minority stake in the 905 MW Aspen portfolio, and US$153m paid in 2025 with about US$280m scheduled for 2026 for the 730 MW portfolios. No percentage is published. Ares's Steven Porto is quoted in the releases; Ares issued no release of its own.

A Vantage executive is quoted in the release. Ares is arranger and lender, not an owner.

relationships.scale: CPP commitment about USD 1.3bn (JPY 193bn) of about USD 2.4bn
relationships.note: CPP Investments is the largest limited partner in Ares's Japan DC Partners I, committing about USD 1.3bn to the fund that Ada Infrastructure builds and operates for.
relationships.context: Ares's release of 11 June 2025 announced the final close of Japan DC Partners I at about USD 2.4bn (JPY 350bn) of equity commitments, for three Greater Tokyo data-centre campuses of nearly 240 MW of IT load developed and operated by Ada Infrastructure, with CPP Investments committing about USD 1.3bn (JPY 193bn). CPP is a fund investor; Ares manages the fund and Ada runs the campuses.

relationships.note: Former co-controller of Prime Data Centers with Ares and Data Realty Group; Macquarie Capital has since sold its remaining stake.
relationships.context: The European Commission's decision M.11843 (18 March 2025) cleared Ares acquiring joint control of Prime Data Centers alongside Wholesale DC Asset Holdings, a Macquarie holding company, and Data Realty Group. Macquarie's FY26 annual report records that Macquarie Capital completed the sale of its remaining stake in Prime; the buyer is not named.

policyExposure.regime: Investment Company Act §36(b) — adviser fee suits
policyExposure.exposure: A derivative action filed on 26 May 2026 in the Southern District of New York on behalf of Ares Capital Corporation alleges that its investment adviser, an Ares subsidiary, received excessive advisory fees in breach of Section 36(b); the adviser disputes the allegations and the case is at a preliminary stage (Ares Capital Q2 2026 filings).

Ares's acquisition of joint control of Prime Data Centers was notified to the European Commission and cleared under the simplified procedure on 18 March 2025 (M.11843); the decision is the only public record of the control structure Ares entered.

Joined Ares in 2015 through its acquisition of Energy Investors Funds, where he had been a partner for ten years; earlier PSEG Power corporate development
Board member of portfolio companies including Apex Clean Energy (company bio)
BA, Duke University; MBA, The Wharton School

decisionMakers.name: Michael Steele
decisionMakers.title: Partner and Head of Ares Digital Infrastructure
background: Leads the data-centre business that includes Ada Infrastructure; member of the Operating Committee
Joined Ares in 2025 as Global President of GLP Capital Partners, whose sale to Ares he led; earlier a partner at Kirkland & Ellis and Freshfields
LLB and BCom, Bond University

decisionMakers.name: Steven Porto
decisionMakers.title: Partner, Ares Infrastructure Equity; Co-Chief Executive Officer, Ares Core Infrastructure Fund
background: Board member of Prime Data Centers and Apex Clean Energy, among other portfolio companies (company bio)
Formerly GE Energy Financial Services

decisionMakers.name: Brent Canada
decisionMakers.title: Partner and Head of Ares Infrastructure Debt
background: Appointed head of infrastructure debt in June 2026, succeeding Patrick Trears; joined Ares in 2022
Previously a managing director in Deutsche Bank's Americas infrastructure financing (power, renewables, energy and telecom); earlier BlackRock
BA in Economics, University of California, Berkeley; CFA

financials.commentary: Company figures from Ares's 10-K, 10-Q and earnings releases; consensus from Zacks via The Globe and Mail and Yahoo Finance. Ares's only stated 2026 expectation is over USD 350m of realized net performance income (8-K, 31 March 2026); its preliminary figures put the first three quarters at about USD 136m. Q3 2026 results are due on 29 October 2026.
